definitions.explanation: A spicy condiment made by infusing vegetable oil with chili peppers. Commonly used in Chinese and Japanese cooking as a topping or seasoning.

examples.japanese: ラー{油|ゆ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦かける→かける：00854_kakeru⟧。
examples.english: I drizzle chili oil on it.

examples.japanese: ⟦{餃子|ぎょうざ}→餃子：08634_gyouza⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ラー{油|ゆ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦つけて→つける：00562_tsukeru⟧⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: I eat gyoza dipped in chili oil.

examples.japanese: ⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧ラー{油|ゆ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ブーム→ブーム：05511_buumu⟧になって、⟦どこ→どこ：00539_doko⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦スーパー→スーパー：01061_suupaa⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{売|う}り{切|き}れていた→売り切れる：03012_urikireru⟧。
examples.english: Crunchy chili oil became a craze and was sold out at every supermarket.

notes:
ラー{油|ゆ} comes from Chinese {辣油|らーゆ} (làyóu). It is a staple condiment in Japanese households, commonly placed on the table alongside soy sauce and vinegar for Chinese-style dishes.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ラー{油|ゆ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦かける→かける：00854_kakeru⟧: to drizzle chili oil
- ⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧ラー{油|ゆ}: crunchy chili oil (with crispy garlic and onion bits)
- ラー{油|ゆ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦つける→つける：00562_tsukeru⟧: to dip in chili oil

USAGE:
⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧ラー{油|ゆ} ("eating chili oil") became a massive food trend in Japan around 2009-2010. Unlike regular chili oil, it contains crunchy bits of fried garlic and onion and is eaten as a topping.
